creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-16 on two Codex 0.162.1 panes on the devenv (review p2c3tkry84, copy p2c3wp2bvy), both stuck. The daemon kept queuing wheel, motion and click reports for them after they stopped reading: draining their terminals took 109 KB and 245 KB of SGR mouse reports, refilling within two seconds of each drain until the daemon's queue (QUEUE_DEPTH, 1024 inputs, each wheel expanding to a report per row) emptied.

Two things go wrong. Mouse reports are stale within a second, so a program that recovers gets minutes of old scrolling and clicks replayed at it. And when the program ends instead, its shell reads the backlog as typed text: the review pane's prompt showed `;50M<35;43;50M27u` as Codex exited, and a report that happens to end in a Return would run a command.

Wheel and motion reports could be dropped instead of queued while a pane reads stuck, and dropped from the queue when it goes stuck. Keys, pastes and pane send text are a separate decision, since a person may mean them. Whatever restarts a stuck agent (a_2dmIEdCn6) has to flush the terminal's input before the program exits.
title: 🖱️ Mouse input keeps queuing for a program that has stopped reading, and lands on whatever reads next
